text:
maya: heads-up — after yesterday's RBAC tidy (PR #4577) we have gaps in KMS audit events from onprem EU nodes :eyes: linking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1229
cheng: which gaps exactly? do you mean missing Decrypt/Encrypt logs or whole request traces?
maya: missing Encrypt/Decrypt entries in keystore-audit. Example (sanitized):
```
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z keystore-proxy request id=abc123 svcacc=svc-infer-eu op=GetKey status=200
# expected later: kms.Decrypt called by svcacc-> but nothing in kms-audit for abc123
```
maya: this started right after the RBAC role-binding change that replaced group:name -> group:infra-ops in EU onprem cluster.
linus: that rings a bell — the keystore proxy maps k8s serviceaccount -> KMS principal via the group membership check. If the binding uses a different group string, the proxy falls back to the non-augmented principal (no KMS policy).
linus: quick repro: if service-account loses `role:keystore-decrypt` binding, we still serve tokens but KMS calls fail silently (proxy swallow) and we still return cached blobs -> audit gap.
eva: also saw that the control-plane netpol for the onprem EU rollout blocks egress to our SIEM collector on port 443 from the audit sidecar in some namespaces. so even if KMS emitted events, they might be dropped. run `kubectl -n infra-audits get netpol -o yaml` to confirm.
maya: pasted minimal diff from PR #4577 that touched clusterrolebinding: 
```diff
- subjects:
- - kind: Group
-   name: old-ops-group
+ subjects:
+ - kind: Group
+   name: infra-ops
```
maya: I think two simultaneous issues: RBAC rename -> wrong principal mapping, AND tightened netpol -> telemetry egress blocked. explains why some requests show no KMS trace and others show KMS logs but SIEM has gaps.
sec-bot: ALERT SEC-1229: 36 affected pods detected in eu-onprem (keystore-proxy). Severity: medium. Recommended actions: apply temporary role-binding mapping, re-enable audit egress.
linus: mitigation plan (short):
1) revert the group rename in RBAC (rollback PR #4577) OR add a temporary ClusterRoleBinding duplicating the old group name to the same subjects.
2) add a keystore-proxy shim policy that forces principal mapping for svcacc `svc-infer-*` (quick patch in configmap).
3) relax netpol in infra-audits namespace to allow egress to siem.redwood.internal:443 (temporary).
4) trigger keystore-proxy restart to force re-sync and re-emit missing events (we have a replay endpoint to re-pad audit entries).
linus: example kubectl to add binding: 
```bash
kubectl create clusterrolebinding temp-keystore-oldgroup --clusterrole=keystore-decrypt --group=old-ops-group --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
cheng: timeline/impact? we need compliance signoff before touching production RBAC. If rollback is easier reticket for change control. Also, which customers might see silent failures vs degraded latency?
maya: initial estimate: 36 pods, impact to inference calls is mostly silent (uses cache) for ~0.5% of requests in EU onprem; some customers will only see audit holes, not functional errors. I'll open an incident page and notify legal/compliance.
eva: add me on the compliance thread. I'll validate netpol exceptions and SIEM ingestion after rollback.
maya: I'll open a mitigation PR to add the temporary binding and the netpol exception, and include steps to run the replay job. pinging @cheng & @linus for review.
cheng: ACK, will review within the hour. please include an audit log snapshot and a signed-off rollback runbook.
linus: after patch, run this quick check: 
```bash
# confirm KMS audit present for a test request
kubectl exec -n inference $(kubectl get pod -l app=svc-infer-eu -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"audit test"}' | jq .id
# then grep SIEM for that request id
```
maya: thanks — I'll update SEC-1229 with the remediation PR and timeline.
(emoji reactions: :hammer: from linus, :eyes: from cheng)
